title: Operational GovOps can halt the surplus distribution if it disputes Spark's rebate calculation
content:
A.6.1.1.1.2.3.2.2.1.2.1.3 gives the reviewer real power: "Operational GovOps reviews Spark's calculation of the rebate before executing a return of surplus to token holders. In the event of any issues, Operational GovOps **cannot** execute the distribution."

Note the phrasing — not "may withhold" but cannot execute. The reviewer is prohibited from proceeding on a calculation it considers defective, which removes the option of paying out under protest and converts the review into a hard gate on money leaving.

The rest of the provision keeps that gate from becoming an indefinite freeze. If the distribution is not executed, Operational GovOps "must post an explanation on the Sky Forum under the 'Spark Prime' category and work with Spark to resolve the disagreement," and unresolved disagreements "must be escalated to Core GovOps."

The result is a three-step ladder: block, explain publicly, escalate to the parent ecosystem's process. Each step limits a different failure. The block prevents an incorrect payout, the public explanation prevents a silent veto, and mandatory escalation prevents a stalemate where neither party can move and token holders simply stop being paid.

The structural point is that Sky places the withholding power with an operational role rather than with a vote — a calculation dispute is resolved by review and escalation, not by an electorate.
description: A disagreement blocks the payout, forces a public explanation on the Sky Forum, and escalates to Core GovOps if the two parties cannot resolve it — a three-step deadlock ladder.
